full_text:
Amaravati, Nov. 18: The India Meteorological Department has reportedly issued a red alert for seven Andhra Pradesh districts as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast.
The affected districts include Kakinada-Yanam, East Godavari, Konaseema, Eluru, West Godavari, Krishna and Bapatla.
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast for Thursday and Friday. Residents have been advised to remain alert as strong winds and rough weather threaten coastal areas.
Cyclone Akvan Moves Towards Andhra Pradesh Coast
According to the supplied weather report, Cyclone Akvan has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm.
The system is reportedly moving slowly at around 3 km per hour. It was located approximately 580 km east of Chennai.

The storm was also around 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.
The cyclone is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. It may make landfall near Kakinada, between Nellore and Visakhapatnam.
The system could intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning.
Weather conditions are expected to deteriorate across North Coastal Andhra Pradesh from Thursday afternoon. Ports in the region remain under the second-stage warning signal.
Winds May Reach 145 Kmph
The weather department has warned of strong winds and heavy rainfall across coastal districts.
Wind speeds could reach 145 mph, creating dangerous conditions in coastal areas.
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is expected in several districts on Thursday and Friday. Residents in low-lying areas have been advised to follow official weather warnings.
Cyclone Akvan | More Districts Likely to Receive Heavy Rainfall
Apart from the seven districts under red alert, several other districts may experience intense rainfall.
Vijayanagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore are likely to receive heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Thursday.
Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, NTR, Palnadu and Tirupati districts are also expected to receive heavy rainfall.
The weather department has reportedly upgraded alerts for Alluri Sitarama Raju, NTR and Palnadu districts from yellow to orange.
Residents Advised to Follow Safety Instructions
Authorities have urged people in affected districts to remain cautious as the cyclone approaches.
Heavy rainfall and strong winds could disrupt normal activities. Coastal areas may also face difficult weather conditions.

Residents should avoid unnecessary travel during severe weather. They should stay away from flooded roads and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
People are advised to monitor official weather bulletins as the cyclone moves closer to the Andhra Pradesh coastline.
